children: Meta (META) plans to sell about $95–97.5B in shares to fund AI infrastructure. After-hours trade was mostly flat; intraday moves were muted. Stock down over 4% for the week, fifth weekly decline.
Meta priced about $25B of Class A shares via forward sales at $625, raising total planned equity to ~$97.5B; proceeds tied to infrastructure, including the Hyperion 5GW Louisiana data center campus.
S&P cut Meta Platforms (META) outlook to negative due to big AI-driven capex ($135–145B), projected free cash flow shortfalls through 2028 and rising adjusted leverage possibly above 1.0x by 2027
Nvidia to invest $3B in Meta Platforms Class A (META) equity; deal expands collaboration to optimize Meta’s Muse AI training/inference and deploy Nvidia hardware in Meta’s AI infrastructure.
Meta (META) plans an at-the-market offering up to $60B once new non-voting Class C shares trade in early 2027 to fund data center and infrastructure investments.
META posted quarterly cash burn after earlier free cash flow. It holds about $134B in servers/equipment and recorded over $14B in asset write-downs through nine months.
META expands Nvidia Vera Rubin chips, Vera CPUs, Spectrum-X networking and BlueField-4 across AI compute and infrastructure; Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom may buy up to $5B in META shares.
Meta Platforms (META) sold shares, boosting its balance sheet and improving standing with bondholders, who are noted as relying on the stronger financial position.
Meta Platforms (META) will cover its AI computing costs, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in October. He suggested broad AI adoption could lead other firms to pay for Meta’s compute capacity.
London High Court upheld Ofcom’s power to force Meta Platforms Class A to hand over moderation data — removed/limited post counts and user exposure metrics — under the Online Safety Act.
